issues: React hydration warning: <span> cannot be a child of <option>. Cause: Emergent build injects x-* debug wrapper spans inside the dynamic <option> children of the LOAD TO SCORE <select>. It's a dev-only warning from the build tooling (not from the app source code) and doesn't break functionality — the select still opens and Load selection works. Non-blocking; framework-level.

critical_code_review_comments: dispatch_autopilot.py:548 _autopilot_cycle_impl — first inner `for ld in fresh:` loop calls `await auto_offer(ld['load_id'])` which relies on FastAPI Depends and will not actually execute (auto_offer is a route handler expecting Depends() injection). The dev is aware (comment on line 578 says '^ won't work due to Depends. Inline the logic instead') and the working inline logic follows immediately. Behaviour is CORRECT because the second loop does the real work, but the dead call to auto_offer is a wasted no-op that still executes score_load through the same broken path and quietly returns without side-effects. Recommend removing the dead call to eliminate confusion and the extra DB read. NON-BLOCKING.
dispatch_autopilot.py:401 sort — qualified.sort uses (-score, -margin_usd); when scores tie AND margins tie you get insertion order. Fine at current scale.

dispatch_ml.py:462 predict — ranked list is sorted by ml_expected_value_usd desc which can produce NEGATIVE margins at the top when the ML rate suggestion exceeds the load's paying rate (documented behaviour per task note). Consider surfacing an `unprofitable: true` flag on rows where ml_expected_margin_usd < 0 so the UI can badge them; today the UI only shows the number. Optional enhancement.

dispatch_ml.py:342 train — accept_auc computes on a 0.25 stratified holdout; with the sharp synthetic rule (line 246) the classifier essentially memorises the boundary → AUC ~0.94. That's expected for synthetic data; production data will land lower. No action needed.

Frontend DispatchAutopilot.jsx:561 — dynamic <option>{l.origin} → {l.destination}</option> generates wrapper <span> elements inside <option> from the emergent build injector. Not a source-code bug; a framework artefact.

dispatch_autopilot.py:459 auto_offer — score_load is called via `await score_load(load_id)` from inside auto_offer, which also relies on Depends() injection. Empirically the tests pass because `_=Depends(get_current_user)` in score_load evaluates to None when called directly and FastAPI's Depends() short-circuits under await from within the same request scope. Works by happy coincidence — cleaner refactor would be to factor _score_load_impl() as a plain async helper called by both.
